description: Weighted cross-domain unlock graph for the ctrl program (and the sediment sibling repo). Consumed by `./ctrl synergy`. Domain edges say how strongly results in domain A tend to unlock work in domain B. Idea edges connect concrete idea IDs from AGENT_IDEA_INDEX.json and candidate IDs below. scoring.description: score = readiness * confidence * (w_nov*novelty/3 + w_app*applicability/3 + w_pay*payoff/5 + w_unlock*tanh(unlock_in/1.5) + w_out*tanh(unlock_out/1.5) + w_pull*pull) - w_eff*log1p(effort_weeks)/log1p(26). unlock_in = sum of incoming idea-edge weights from ready_to_use nodes; unlock_out = sum of outgoing weights; pull = 1.0 for bounty/customer/grant, 0.7 for a standard or certification, 0.4 for community demand, 0 for none. For candidates readiness = 0.6 + 0.4 * mean readiness of builds_on (SED counts 0.8). With --goal, score is multiplied by 0.25 + 0.75*keyword_overlap(goal, node text); with --domain, by 0.25 + 0.75*max domain->domain weight into the target domains. Readiness: ready_to_use 1.0, promising_near_complete 0.85, in_work 0.7, candidate 0.6.
scoring.rationale: Payoff and unlock-in dominate so that cheap work sitting one edge away from a READY node outranks ambitious isolated work; effort is log-damped so a 12-week project is not crushed, just discounted.

candidates.title: Geometric SO(3)/SE(3) tracking certificate (Lee-Leok-McClamroch)
candidates.why_now: ISO 25785-1 (actively balanced robots) and drone RTA standards now ask for stability evidence; the July-2026 Lean control paper (arXiv 2607.19727) covers Lyapunov/small-gain but nothing on Lie groups, so SE(3) geometric control is the open Lean niche.
candidates.prior_art: Paper proofs only (Lee-Leok-McClamroch 2010/2013, Goodarzi-Lee-Lee PID/adaptive). coq-robot has static SO(3)/SE(3)/screws but no dynamics or Lyapunov; Isabelle AFP Lie groups are abstract; Mathlib LieGroup is abstract. No mechanized geometric tracking controller found.
candidates.missing_capability: Lean theorems: attitude error function Psi(R,Rd)=1/2 tr(I - Rd^T R), error vector e_R, bounds 1/2|e_R|^2 <= Psi <= |e_R|^2/(2-Psi), dPsi/dt = e_R . e_Omega, and exponential convergence of the attitude/position tracking errors on the sublevel set {Psi < 2} for the rigid-body Euler equations; then the C99 kernel ctrl_geometric_so3_pd bound via @lean_theorem.
candidates.external_pull: Drone/quadrotor industry and ASTM F3269 RTA; humanoid balance (ISO/CD 25785-1 working group led by Agility/Boston Dynamics)

candidates.title: Invariant EKF: group-affine dynamics imply log-linear error on SE(3)/SE_2(3)
candidates.why_now: 2025 work (arXiv 2506.01514) settled left/right-invariant equivalence under covariance reset, and contact-aided invariant EKFs are the de facto legged-robot estimator; no proof assistant has the core Barrau-Bonnabel theorem.
candidates.prior_art: Barrau-Bonnabel (TAC) paper proofs; Isabelle AFP Lie Groups (abstract, no filtering); ctrl EST-01 is Euclidean Kalman. No mechanization found.
candidates.missing_capability: Lean: definition of group-affine vector fields on matrix Lie groups (concrete SE(3) and SE_2(3) as 4x4/5x5 matrices), theorem that the invariant error eta = Xhat X^-1 obeys an autonomous ODE independent of the trajectory, the linearized error equation in the Lie algebra via adjoint6, and the resulting trajectory-independent Riccati equation; a Python/C99 IEKF kernel bound to these theorems.
candidates.external_pull: Legged/humanoid state estimation (contact-aided InEKF), VIO/SLAM consistency community (OpenVINS)

cross_domain_edge.why: SE3Kinematics adjoint functoriality is exactly the algebra that makes the IEKF error dynamics linear.

candidates.title: VIO observability: 4-dim unobservable subspace and FEJ consistency theorem
candidates.why_now: FEJ/OC-EKF are standard in every production VIO (OpenVINS, MSCKF) but the nullspace-preservation argument exists only as paper linear algebra; ctrl's dual-annihilator Observability.lean is the exact tool to state it coordinate-free.
candidates.prior_art: Kottas et al. ISER 2012, Li-Mourikis IJRR 2013, OpenVINS FEJ documentation; no proof-assistant formalization.
candidates.missing_capability: Lean theorems: for the linearized IMU-camera error model, the explicit 4-column nullspace (global position, rotation about gravity) lies in the kernel of the observability matrix; evaluating Jacobians at first estimates preserves this kernel (FEJ), and naive re-linearization strictly shrinks it (the inconsistency counterexample as a theorem).
candidates.external_pull: OpenVINS/MSCKF community; AR/VR and drone VIO vendors who need consistency arguments

cross_domain_edge.why: Coordinate-free observability from CTRL-05 turns a VIO folklore result into a theorem.

candidates.why_now: InformationFilter.lean already proves the SMW precision equivalence; 2024-2026 distributed invariant KF and adaptive Kalman-consensus work shows ongoing demand, and nobody has a mechanised proof that information-form fusion of independent measurements is additive and consistent.
candidates.prior_art: Casbeer-Beard information consensus filter; Li-Huang-Hu ICF vs KCF comparison; Zhu-Ren fully distributed localisation; UCLA LEMUR covariance intersection. No proof-assistant versions.
candidates.missing_capability: Lean theorems: additivity of information contributions across agents, equivalence to the centralised Joseph update, and a conservative (covariance-intersection) bound under unknown correlation; `ctrl_info_fusion` C99 kernel and a multi-robot localisation benchmark.
candidates.external_pull: multi-robot localisation community; AMR vendors

cross_domain_edge.why: Information form is the only filter form whose fusion is a sum, which is what communication-limited fleets need.

candidates.title: Homography ground plane to tilted ZMP/CBF deceleration bound
candidates.why_now: Perceptive legged locomotion (2025-2026 MIQP on depth-derived steppable regions) now estimates terrain planes online, but the safety bound is always re-solved numerically; the repo's closed-form bound assumes a flat ground and the 4-point homography uniqueness gives the plane normal for free.
candidates.prior_art: Ground-plane homography (Hartley-Zisserman style), Dragon-Van Gool CVPR14, Fallon et al. Atlas 2015 planar segmentation, 2026 perceptive MIQP footstep planning; none derives a closed-form inclined-plane deceleration/ZMP bound from a homography.
candidates.missing_capability: Lean theorem: given the plane normal n from homography decomposition (HomographyDecomposition.lean), the safe deceleration bound becomes a_max(theta)=min(mu cos theta - sin theta, (W/h_G)cos theta - ...)g on a slope, with forward invariance of the corresponding Lorentz-cone CBF; MuJoCo quadruped-on-ramp benchmark with a camera.
candidates.external_pull: legged-robot vendors (perceptive locomotion); no bounty

cross_domain_edge.why: The homography's plane normal is the one scalar the closed-form ZMP bound is missing on non-flat ground.

candidates.title: Syntactic WCET bound of generated C99 kernels fed into RTA
candidates.why_now: rocq-prosa v0.6 (Oct 2025) makes verified RTA mainstream but takes WCET as an oracle; DO-178C 6.3.4f WCET objectives and tool-qualification pressure (Rapita, AbsInt) make a machine-checked 'kernel -> C_i -> schedulable' chain a differentiator; the repo's kernels are straight-line and zero-heap, the easy case.
candidates.prior_art: Prosa abstract RTA (Bozhko-Brandenburg), RT-CertiKOS+Prosa (CAV19), Velus/CompCert verified Lustre-to-C, AbsInt aiT and Rapita RapiTime (qualified tools). None links a theorem-prover codegen's output structure to the C_i used by a verified RTA.
candidates.missing_capability: A Lean-side cost model over the codegen AST (op count, no loops/heap) yielding a per-kernel instruction-count bound, a theorem that the bound is monotone under the kernel composition used in the quadruped shield, and a response_time_analysis instance consuming those bounds; produce a DO-178C-style evidence bundle (bound, measurement on target, qualification narrative).
candidates.external_pull: certification bodies (DO-178C, IEC 61508/61131-3 PLC users); potential paying customers in PLC/robotics safety

cross_domain_edge.why: RTA has no input without C_i, and zero-heap straight-line codegen is the one case where C_i can be proved rather than measured.

candidates.title: Cross-ratio fiducial detection with Reed-Solomon coded identity
candidates.why_now: Learned tag families (E2ETag) and projective-invariant tags (Pi-Tag, X-tag) coexist with AprilTag's Hamming-table decoding; a verified pipeline that uses the cross-ratio for detection and an RS code for ID has no formal counterpart and reuses two READY modules.
candidates.prior_art: Pi-Tag (Bergamasco et al. 2011, cross-ratio detection), X-tag (Birdal 2016), AprilTag 2 (code tables), RUNE-tag; cross-ratio known to be noise-sensitive so only a few configurations are distinguishable.
candidates.missing_capability: Lean theorem that cross-ratio invariance (CrossRatio.lean) plus an RS(n,k) code on the bit pattern gives a decoding with provable false-positive bound given the known cross-ratio noise sensitivity; Python/C99 decoder; honest benchmark against AprilTag on synthetic perspective views.
candidates.external_pull: weak: AprilTag dominates; niche interest in projective-invariant markers

cross_domain_edge.why: Projective invariants supply the geometry, RS codes the identity; the pair is the fiducial.

candidates.title: Barrier-derived Simplex switching for learned controllers
candidates.why_now: Neural Simplex (reverse switching, online retraining), Black-Box Simplex and Bb-Simplex (barrier-certificate switching, 2025-2026) are the current runtime-assurance pattern for RL controllers; the repo has a Lean-verified barrier and a Simplex theorem but no switching condition derived from the barrier.
candidates.prior_art: Sha's Simplex; Phan et al. NSA; Black-Box Simplex (F-16 collision case studies); Bb-Simplex (Taylor-expanded barrier switching for microgrids). No Lean-verified barrier used as the Simplex certificate.
candidates.missing_capability: Lean theorem: the Lorentz-cone CBF sublevel set is a Simplex recoverable region, the switching condition derived from one-step barrier decrease keeps the learned controller active whenever safe, and reverse switching is sound; `ctrl_simplex_barrier_switch` C99 kernel and MuJoCo quadruped benchmark with an RL policy as the advanced controller.
candidates.external_pull: runtime assurance for learning-enabled systems (DARPA Assured Autonomy lineage, UL 4600 context)

cross_domain_edge.why: A closed-form barrier is exactly the certificate that makes Simplex switching cheap and provable.

scoring_proposals.formula: score = conf * (0.20*N + 0.10*A + 0.15*R + 0.25*U + 0.15*P + 0.15*(1-E)); N=novelty tier/3; A=applicability tier/3; R=mean readiness of builds_on (ready 1, promising 0.6, in_work 0.3, SED 0.8); U=min(1, sum over READY builds_on r of w_domain(domain(r)->domain(c)) / 2); P=external pull (bounty/customer 1, standard/cert 0.7, community 0.4, none 0); E=min(1, effort_weeks/12); conf in [0,1]
scoring_proposals.rationale: Unlock in-degree from READY nodes carries the most weight because the purpose of the graph is to compound ready assets; saturation at two strong unlockers prevents gaming via long builds_on lists. Novelty outweighs applicability because zero-sorry theorems are the repo's differentiator. Readiness and effort are symmetric so a 2-week productionization of a ready result ties with an 8-week N3 exploration. Confidence multiplies so speculative edges are discounted everywhere.
